I think that `PTRef::Analyze()` should be able to properly handle the case when it referenced UDT field, not table column. This is by far more logical than doing `if (key->opcode() != TreeNodeOpcode::kPTRef)` special case exception in `Analyze` of higher-level  expression.

Also, I'm not sure that `token({a:1})` is a valid syntax at all, since we don't (or not always, for other functions?) have UDT schema for reference

issue.title: [YCQL] Referencing column in UPDATE for UDT crashes tserver

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-4708](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-4708)
Given the schema:
```cql
CREATE TYPE k.udt_ab (a int, b text);
CREATE TABLE k.cd(c int PRIMARY KEY, d udt_ab);
INSERT INTO k.cd(c, d) VALUES (1, {a: 10, b: 'foo'});
```
This crashes server:
```cql
UPDATE k.cd SET d = {a: c, b: 'bar'} WHERE c = 1;
```
Stack trace:
```

```
